correctness.rationale: The exact integer matrix Q^10-I=X has X^2 divisible by 11, X^3/11 congruent to 7(X mod11), and Q(X mod11)=7(X mod11), producing ten distinct gap residues and a unit quadratic coefficient in every branch. Integral convergence of the Mahler tail is proved using v_11(X^i)>=floor(i/2) and factorial bounds. Each analytic branch has exactly one nondegenerate critical point, and a globally bijective isometry conjugates it to a translated scaled square. This implies the complete all-depth residue and fiber formulas; Haar measure follows from a geometric series. The packaged Python checker verifies matrix identities and all residue histograms through the fifth 11-power, but finite tests are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The natural lag-ten Tribonacci gap at the exceptional ramified prime eleven was known to have a short period, but a period does not determine represented values. The new complete ten-sheet image classification, every target fiber, the 5/12 Haar measure, and the critical-value obstruction give a precise all-depth local arithmetic invariant. The quadratic branch decomposition is structurally useful for representation and lifting, not an arbitrary finite computation.
